questions.problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(-2,5,-3)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨1,-1,2⟩.$ Find all the possible points $A$ on that line such that $AP=\sqrt{24}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨-2,5,-3⟩+t⟨1,-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Since $A$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OA} & =⟨-2,5,-3⟩+t⟨1,-1,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PA} & =\overset{\to }{OA}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨-2,5,-3⟩+t⟨1,-1,2⟩)-⟨-2,5,-3⟩ \\  & =t\,⟨1,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨t,\,-t,\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PA=\sqrt{24},$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}AP & =\sqrt{24} \\ |\overset{\to }{PA}| & =\sqrt{24} \\ |⟨t,\,-t,\,2t⟩| & =\sqrt{24} \\ \sqrt{{t}^{2}+(-t)^{2}+(2t)^{2}} & =\sqrt{24} \\ \sqrt{6{t}^{2}} & =\sqrt{24} \\ \pm t\sqrt{6} & =2\sqrt{6} \\ t & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm 2$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{1}}=⟨-2,5,-3⟩+2⟨1,-1,2⟩=⟨0,3,1⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{2}}=⟨-2,5,-3⟩-2⟨1,-1,2⟩=⟨-4,7,-7⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are ${A}_{1}(0,3,1)$ and ${A}_{2}(-4,7,-7).$

questions.problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(-4,2,-3)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩.$ Find all the possible points $X$ on that line such that $XP=\sqrt{20}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨-4,\,2,\,-3⟩+t⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Since $X$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OX} & =⟨-4,\,2,\,-3⟩+t⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PX} & =\overset{\to }{OX}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨-4,\,2,\,-3⟩+t⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩)-⟨-4,\,2,\,-3⟩ \\  & =t⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨t,\,0,\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PX=\sqrt{20},$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}XP & =\sqrt{20} \\ |\overset{\to }{PX}| & =\sqrt{20} \\ |⟨t,\,0,\,2t⟩| & =\sqrt{20} \\ \sqrt{{t}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(2t)^{2}} & =\sqrt{20} \\ \sqrt{5{t}^{2}} & =\sqrt{20} \\ \pm \sqrt{5}t & =2\sqrt{5} \\ t & =\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm 2$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{X}_{1}}=⟨-4,\,2,\,-3⟩+2⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩=⟨-2,2,1⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{X}_{2}}=⟨-4,\,2,\,-3⟩-2⟨1,\,0,\,2⟩=⟨-6,2,-7⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are ${X}_{1}(-2,2,1)$ and ${X}_{2}(-6,2,-7).$

questions.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $H(1,-2,3)$ and $S(4,-2,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $H$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=h+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $h$ is the position vector of $H.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $H(1,-2,3)$ and $S(4,-2,1),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{HS} \\  & =⟨4,-2,1⟩-⟨1,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,0,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The equation below gives a parametrization of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(1,0,3)$ and $Q(1,2,0).$

$$
r(t)=i+a\,j+b\,k,\,t\in [c,1]
$$

What is $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(i+2\,j)-(i+3\,k) \\  & =2\,j-3\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
r=p+tv\,⟹\,r=(i+3\,k)+t(2\,j-3\,k)
$$

and the parametrization of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(i+3\,k)+t(2\,j-3\,k) \\  & =i+2t\,j+(3-3t)\,k,\,t\in [0,1].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=2t+(3-3t)+0=3-t.
$$

questions.problem:
The equation below describes all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(-6,2,-1)$ and $Q(-8,0,-1).$

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2 \\ a\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ b \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,t\in [0,c]
$$

What is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
r=p+tv\,⟹\,r=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

and the vector equation of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ is

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,t\in [0,1].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=(-1)+(-2)+1=-2.
$$
